title: Clean batches of raw numbers with a reference-only pipeline

blocks.text: A method reference passes its argument on unchanged: `Integer::parseInt` cannot trim `"  42  "` first. The page's fix is a separate step, `map(String::trim)`, before it. A reference cannot be negated with `!` either; `Predicate.not(String::isBlank)` can.

Write `NumberCleaner.clean(List<List<String>> batches)`. It reads every entry of every batch, skips `null` and blank entries, parses the rest as integers (ignoring spaces around them), removes repeated numbers and returns them **highest first**. Use method references for every step that only calls a method (`Collection::stream` flattens the batches in `flatMap`).
A number can be written more than one way.

cases.says: It flattens the batches, parses the numbers, drops repeats and sorts them highest first.
Integer::parseInt cannot adapt its argument, so a String::trim step comes before it.
Nulls and entries of spaces only are skipped; an isEmpty check before trimming lets spaces through.
"7", " 7" and "07" are one number, so repeats are removed after parsing, not before.
Repeats are found with equals, so 1000 read twice counts once even though each parse makes its own Integer.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A reference cannot adapt its argument, so a separate String::trim step runs before Integer::parseInt.
Collection::stream in flatMap turns a list of lists into one stream.
